summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of systolic heart failure (LVEF 20%), ischemic cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and obesity, was admitted due to acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbation caused by medication non-adherence. He had stopped taking his full dose of torsemide after running out of tablets, leading to 13 pounds of fluid gain, worsening shortness of breath, and pulmonary edema seen on chest X-ray. He was treated with IV furosemide and resumed his home dose of torsemide, resulting in significant diuresis and symptom improvement. His weight decreased from 139.1 kg to 133.6 kg over three days. All chronic medications were continued, with metoprolol restarted on hospital day two. He was discharged home in stable condition with strict instructions to adhere to his medication regimen and monitor daily weight.
